Pasadena roofing contractors work under two sets of rules

Hiring among Pasadena roofing contractors starts with one map question: is your house east or west of State Highway 146? Most of the city lies west of it and follows ordinary city permit rules. The slice east of the highway is part of the state's coastal windstorm area, and a new roof there has to pass inspections the rest of Pasadena never sees.

Both halves share the same weather. Pasadena sits in southeast Harris County, south of the Houston Ship Channel, and much of it drains to Vince Bayou, Little Vince Bayou or Armand Bayou, all of them Harris County Flood Control District watersheds. Gulf storms, summer squall lines and the occasional derecho reach it with little to slow them down.

Houston Expert Roofers is not one of those contractors. It is a free phone line. A recorded assistant picks up, asks what the roof is doing, and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in Pasadena. That company inspects, quotes and does the job.

East or west of State Highway 146: what changes for your roof

In a Commissioner's Order dated December 1996, the Texas Department of Insurance designated the parts of Pasadena and Shoreacres east of State Highway 146 as catastrophe areas. A TDI bulletin says the designation took effect March 1, 1997. TDI's Harris County windstorm page still lists Pasadena with La Porte, Morgan's Point, Seabrook and Shoreacres.

QuestionWest of SH 146 (most of Pasadena)East of SH 146, inside city limits
City roofing permitRequired when work covers more than 25 percent of a roofSame city rule
Windstorm building codeNot part of the TDI programRoof work must meet it
Inspection during installationCity inspection only, where a permit appliesWindstorm inspection while the roof goes on, plus the city's
Paper to keepPermit, contract, invoice, shingle warranty registrationAll of those plus the WPI-8 certificate of compliance
Who insures windYour regular homeowners policyYour policy, or a Texas Windstorm Insurance Association policy where private wind coverage is not available

Not sure which side you are on? TDI's maps are general guides, and the agency asks owners to verify an exact address. Its Windstorm Inspections office takes calls at 1-800-248-6032 (option 4). Settle the question before you sign, because adding a windstorm inspection after the shingles are on is not possible.

The City of Pasadena roofing permit, in plain terms

Pasadena's posted fee schedule sets out three rules that matter to anyone hiring a roofer:

  • The 25 percent trigger. Replacing or repairing more than 25 percent of each roof needs a permit. A full tear-off always crosses that line; a handful of replaced shingles usually does not.
  • A flat residential fee. The schedule lists one residential roofing permit fee per structure, covering an overlay or replacement with like materials plus minor decking and structural work approved by the building inspector or plan reviewer. Confirm the current amount with the city, since fee schedules change.
  • No new wood shakes. Wood shingles, shakes and other combustible roofing are prohibited in any roofing project, except minor repairs to existing single-family homes.

The Permit Department works from City Hall at 1149 Ellsworth, on weekday business hours, and the city says no permits are issued after 4:30 p.m. Its permit line is 713-475-5575. Commercial roofs follow a separate fee, and the city asks for engineered drawings when a commercial roof is altered or structurally changed, which matters to owners of shops and offices as well as homes.

A roofer that works Pasadena regularly will pull the permit in its own name. If a contractor asks you to apply as the owner, or says a full replacement "does not need anything," ask why, and get the answer in writing.

Storms that shaped Pasadena roofs

The last decade gave Pasadena roofs a hard run. Each storm below is documented by a public agency or by local reporting, and each left the kind of damage a roofer looks for years later.

  1. Hurricane Harvey, August 2017. Harvey is remembered for rain more than wind. The Harris County Flood Control District counts roughly 120,000 flooded structures across the region, and Pasadena's bayous were part of that. For roofs, days of rain found every cracked boot and loose flashing joint.
  2. The derecho, May 16, 2024. The National Weather Service office in League City describes a swath of winds over 100 mph across the Houston metro. Lines of storms like that lift shingle tabs across whole neighborhoods at once.
  3. Hurricane Beryl, July 8, 2024. Beryl reached the Texas coast as a Category 1 storm and knocked out power to more than two million CenterPoint Energy customers. Torn shingles, fallen limbs and bent gutters were common across east Harris County.

A shingle whose seal broke in 2024 can lie flat and look normal from the street, then let wind-driven rain underneath in the next squall. If your roof has not been looked at since Beryl, and you see granules piling at the downspouts or a new ceiling stain, it is worth a call. The wind damage page shows what to look for from the ground.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Why Pasadena homeowners call the line

The highway line is easy to get wrong

A contractor who mostly works west of SH 146 may not plan for a windstorm inspection. When you call, say which side of the highway you are on, and ask the company you reach how it schedules the inspection and delivers the WPI-8.

Shake roofs and old decking

Because the city bars new wood shakes, a house still wearing them needs a different covering, and the boards underneath may need work first. A roofer that knows older Pasadena houses expects that and prices decking per sheet before it starts.

Storm crews come and go

After a big storm, strangers with roofing offers often knock on doors. You do not have to hire whoever shows up. The line connects you with a locally owned company instead, one you can reach again with a question about the warranty.

One number at 2 a.m.

Water through a ceiling does not wait for business hours. Calls to (832) 662-4107 reach an automated assistant around the clock, and if the roofer cannot pick up, it passes along your name, number and the problem for a call back.

Questions to put to Pasadena roofing companies

Rules and paperwork

  • Is my address east or west of SH 146, and how did you check?
  • Will you pull the city permit, and when will I see the permit number?
  • If I am in the windstorm area, who schedules the inspection, and when do I get the WPI-8?
  • Can you send your certificate of liability insurance directly to me?

The roof itself

  • How many layers are on the roof now, and will every one come off?
  • What is the price per sheet if the decking is soft or the boards are gapped?
  • Which underlayment, drip edge and flashing are in the price, by name?
  • Will you register the shingle warranty, and what does your workmanship warranty cover in writing?

If an insurer may pay for the roof, read the roof insurance claims guide before signing anything. You file the claim, not the roofer.

How a Pasadena roofing call works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), most roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way (TDI exempts repairs to less than 100 square feet of roof covering that do not touch the decking). When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Do Pasadena roofing contractors need a city permit for a new roof?

Usually, yes. The City of Pasadena's fee schedule says roof replacement or repairs covering more than 25 percent of each roof require a permit, and it lists a residential roofing permit fee per structure for overlays and like-for-like replacement with minor decking work. A small patch below that threshold generally does not need one. Ask the contractor to pull the permit in its own name and show it to you. The roof replacement page covers what the job should include.

Does a new roof in Pasadena, TX need a windstorm inspection?

Only if the house is inside Pasadena city limits and east of State Highway 146. The Texas Department of Insurance added that part of the city to its designated catastrophe area, effective March 1, 1997. Roof work there is built to the windstorm code and inspected while it is under way, and the home gets a WPI-8 certificate of compliance, which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses for eligibility. West of SH 146 the program does not apply.

Can I put a wood shake roof on my Pasadena house?

Not as a new roof. The city's fee schedule says wood shingles, shakes and other combustible roofing materials are prohibited in any type of roofing project, except minor repairs to existing single-family homes. If your house still has wood shakes, plan on asphalt shingles, metal or another approved covering when it is replaced, and expect the roofer to look closely at the decking under the shakes. See metal roofing for one option.

How do I check whether a Pasadena roofer is legitimate?

Texas has no state roofing license, so check what you can. Ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent straight to you, a written contract with the full scope, and the city permit number. Drive past a couple of roofs the company did nearby. Never accept an offer to cover your insurance deductible, which Texas law forbids. The guide do roofers need a license in Texas walks through each check.

Who actually answers when I call from Pasadena?

Whatever the hour, an automated assistant picks up, learns what the roof is doing and where the house sits, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Pasadena calls. That company sets the price, inspects and handles the job, and you are its customer, paying it yourself. Houston Expert Roofers never charges you; the company may pay the line a referral fee.
